title: Thailand mandates crypto Travel Rule with self-custody wallet verification
dek: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission finalized crypto Travel Rule requirements for digital asset operators, including verification that users control self-hosted wallets and five-year transaction data retention, effective February 2027.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Thailand joins the global Travel Rule enforcement wave, requiring crypto platforms to verify self-custody wallet control and retain transaction records for five years starting February 2027.
bottom_line: Thailand's February 2027 Travel Rule effective date is a compliance deadline for any crypto platform serving Thai users. The requirement to verify self-custody wallet control introduces a new friction point in the user workflow and establishes Thailand as a Travel Rule enforcement jurisdiction in Southeast Asia. How platforms will technically verify wallet control without compromising user privacy will determine whether this regulation remains a procedural check or becomes a practical barrier to self-custody transactions.
body: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission finalized crypto Travel Rule requirements for digital asset operators, effective February 2027, according to Cointelegraph's reporting on September 2.

The requirements include verification that users control self-hosted wallets and mandatory five-year retention of transaction data. Digital asset operators must confirm whether a user sending cryptocurrency to an external address owns that address themselves.

Thailand joins a growing list of jurisdictions adopting Travel Rule compliance frameworks that extend anti-money-laundering scrutiny to self-custody transactions. The self-hosted wallet verification requirement creates a procedural boundary: operators must confirm private-key control before processing certain transfers, adding friction to decentralized transaction flows.

The specific mechanism by which operators are expected to verify self-custody control, the scope of which operators fall under the requirements, and penalties for non-compliance are not detailed in the source reporting.
